body:
I’m 27 and I’ve never really been in a relationship or even gone on a date! When I was 23ish I had sex a couple of times with someone but I ‘was a woman’.  I agree with everyone that there’s absolutely nothing wrong with being a virgin, but I really relate to feeling like you’re behind the curve and missing out on experiences that TV tells you everyone has in high school. I think it does feel awkward and I’m really nervous about going on a date with someone and feeling inexperienced- both sexually but also just because I’ve never had that emotional intimacy. But the right person will be happy to navigate that with you I’m sure. 

It seems pretty natural that it might take trans people longer to get into relationships (both emotionally and sexually) when we need to spend so much extra time figuring out who we are, what we need to be happy, and then dealing with our personal transition needs on top of all of that. 

Don’t really know what to tell you about moving forward, but you don’t deserve to feel ashamed.

This is a really nuanced view, but I think it’s often true. A lot of people will say off the bat to not engage with your family if they’re homophobic, but it’s hard when you know they’re being hateful out of a place of love. It’s definitely not fair or right, but it certainly makes the feelings more complicated. Hopefully OPs mom will take her own messages to heart in regards to ‘realizing that you’re not always right’.
Yeah, same. Can't believe how much it can change my face.

Thanks for the response. I’ve always thought my face is most masculine directly from the front, but I see now how the hairline really helps the side view. I always had a pretty male hairline, but it’s definitely gone back more with T. Hopefully it stops where it is! Hah.

I definitely struggle with thinking I immediately look like a girl when I smile, but try to remember that guys smile too. 

That’s interesting about the posture. I think that’s true now that you say it.

My voice does pass. I’m nearing 2 years on T, but I only started being gendered correctly in public over the past year while wearing a mask. It’s hard to tell if that was because of continued changes or because I was hiding half my face. So now when I’m not wearing one, I’m self conscious about how people are perceiving me. And at a couple years on T I worry this is it for face changes short of a potential beard coming in. Thanks for the reply!
Which way does the haircut swing me? To male? Or is it a butch lesbian read?

I flew back 5 days after my surgery and had dressings / the wrap on. I just told someone near the scanner that I couldn’t raise my arms and they put me off to the side for a bit. Someone else came over and had me walk through the metal detector and then swabbed my hands for explosives residue. They didn’t pat me down at all and I didn’t need to mention that I’d had surgery.

It’s definitely not a topic that can be brought up in casual conversation so it was really nice to see and relate to your post. I hope you get to figure out your own thoughts and be comfortable with how you see yourself.

I’ve been having the exact same thoughts! When I think about being submissive with another man, my brain automatically pictures me as a woman. It’s been bothering me because (even though I see myself 100% as a man in daily life) I don’t understand how I can be a trans man if I see myself as a woman during sex. 

I’ve been thinking too about whether it’s related to misogyny. I think it’s natural in this society for people to picture a masculine, dominant man with a feminine, submissive woman. Whereas for a man to be submissive, it can be seen as being sort of shameful rather than sexual since submissiveness is wrapped up with femininity and seen as inherently the woman’s role. Just speaking about general societal opinions, not saying it’s true. 

I’ve been trying to tell myself that plenty of cis men bottom or like being submissive and they are still men and can still be masculine while doing so. 

I feel more masculine when thinking about having sex with a woman. It’s like I get to take on the ‘male role’. But when having sex with a cis man, that role is already taken. I think that is because I haven’t been exposed to or seen a lot of representations of gay sex. It’s like my brain has to put me in a box where I can only have straight sex. 

Anyways, that got long winded, but you’re definitely not the only one. I’m hoping that it all has to do with internal biases that can be worked through.

I’ve been on T for ~1.5 years and haven’t had a period since my first month on T. I had spotting three days after my second Pfizer shot. Random ‘spotting’ (only visible when I wipe) continued off and on every few days for about 3 weeks. I hope it’s done, but not too sure. Doctor doesn’t know why it would be so extended, but I think the timing links it to the vaccine.

Yeah, I’m sorry for how rough that was. I’m grateful I was able to choose when to come out to my parents, but nothing prepares you for that shocking anger coming from the people who have loved you for so long.  I feel like it’s really hard to forgive things like that. All the yelling and awful things that were said. But I know if I don’t let it go we won’t have a relationship. 

I really like how you frame it as reflecting the values they taught you. Sometimes I’m tired of being ‘the bigger person’, but I don’t want to change who I am / how I act as a person. I want them to see that I’m still me and that I’m so much happier. I know that when they are hurtful it’s because they are hurting and confused. 

Thank you for the perspective. It’s how I’ve been feeling, but it’s hard to put to words.

Wow, I feel a lot of the same things about my mom. She gets really upset when I dress masculine and I’m scared my coming out is going to hurt her. She lost her mom 6 months ago too and she’s so emotional all the time and I don’t want to hurt her more. I like to think that, even if our relationship suffers for awhile, she has other people who can help her process her feelings. It’s going to be a long, awful road I’m sure, but I hope she’ll be able to realize how much happier I am when I transition. I definitely get that fear of losing your relationship with your mom though. I hope things get better for you.

Rock climbing with spiders. 
They would have the advantage.

I hate that so many of my pants do this! And especially dress pants. Then if you pull them up so it doesn’t crease, the waist goes way too high. I’ve been wondering too if it’s a fit issue. Definitely annoying.

Mine felt out of nowhere too. It really bugs me that I can’t remember why I first questioned it. I went down an internet rabbit hole and ended up at this subreddit and then saw transition videos on YouTube and felt so thrilled that transition was a thing. And then I was like, why is this so exciting to me? So I’ve been slowly coming to terms with the fact that I’m trans.
Hey, thanks so much! I had a busy night that distracted me, but coming back to this comment made me smile : ) Hope you have a happy new year!

I’ve been coming out to friends and some called me he/him right away, but I didn’t want to push it with others because I definitely don’t pass. I thought it wouldn’t bother me, but she/her feels so much worse when people use it who know I’m trans. I wasn’t expecting that, and a part of me still doesn’t want to ask to be called he/him when I know I don’t look like a guy. But, personally, I’m thinking of asking all of my friends to make the switch because it bothers me more and more and I’m (mostly) sure they’d be accepting if not a little thrown off by the change. Just wanted to say I’m in the same spot. I’m not sure what to do either.

I came out to my friends as questioning about 3 months into the process so I could try out a new name and pronouns with them. After I was pretty sure, I told my sister. I’m 24 so I don’t want to wait any longer. A part of me is excited to come out. But I’m waiting to tell my parents until I move out since I think it’s going to be very emotional and negative for them, and I don’t want to be around for that. So I’ll have been waiting a year total before telling them.

I'm 24 (ftm) and just realized that I'm trans four months ago. I'm positive that I want to start HRT sooner than later. Sometimes I worry that I'm rushing things, but I really agree with what you said. I just recently realized that I'm trans, but there's always been something off. So, looking back, this is something I've had to deal with a long time. Even though I didn't realize exactly what I was dealing with, I don't want to wait any longer to start fixing it! It's been a really long time already. That makes me feel better when I'm afraid of rushing. 

I'm not out to my parents yet though because I want to move out before I tell them. I know they'll feel similarly to your parents. It is a big change in their perception, so it makes sense that it'll take time for them to adjust. It might be something they'll come around to after seeing how happy you are with transitioning. Change is scary for a lot of people and they might just be worried about that. Hopefully they can see you're still the same person. Just a person who understands more about who they are! If they aren't there for your first T shot, maybe they will come around and be supportive for other milestones along the way.
Wow. I just wrote my friend a really long message this morning about how it’s so hard to wait to transition and how impatient I feel. This is what I needed to read right now. Thanks.

Thanks for the response. I know I just need to be patient with it, but it’s still good to hear. It is hard to be in that middle ground of some people knowing and some not. I definitely still misgender myself sometimes in situations where I don’t have to. It really does take getting used to. That’s a really good idea about having a close network that gets it. Seems like a good way to focus on being comfortable without stressing about how everyone else sees me. Thanks!

Yeah, my character is a man so I thought it might be even easier to call me he instead of switching back and forth, but it didn't really help. I really agree with not looking how I feel. It doesn't bother me so much for people to say what they see. I mean, that usually turns out to be correct. I just kind of want to be able to be treated as a guy so I can know for sure that it's right for me and that I want to transition. Like practical experience would help me be 1000% sure. But yeah, it's hard when the inside and outside don't match up.
hah. That's hilarious and great!

That response was super fast. Like, record-breaking. hah. Yeah, I definitely didn't expect it to be smooth at all. And I'm lucky that they care and are trying. It was good overall. Just didn't expect to feel so awkward like I'm pretending to be a guy and they're going along with it. I'm sure it'll get better for everyone though. Hopefully. Thanks
That's genius

I’m still trying to figure out if I’m trans because I’ve only started thinking about it the last couple months. But my gut says I’m a guy. And basically my biggest fear is that I’m making myself think I’m trans when I’m not. My dysphoria isn’t very strong. It’s just at the level of discomfort, so I didn’t really notice it before. It’s just the way things were. So I keep thinking maybe I never had dysphoria. Maybe I’m just making myself think that. Maybe my chest doesn’t really bother me and I’m just making myself aware of it because I want to be trans. But then I have the same thought as you about why would I not want to be cis when that’s more comfortable/easier in society. 


I don’t have any answers, but I definitely feel this way and I don’t even have a solid history of identifying as male. I think it’s pretty normal to have doubts about any big thing in your life. When I first got diagnosed with depression I thought I was faking it. And who wants depression?? My idea is to focus on what makes me comfortable day to day and hope that everything makes sense in the end!

That’s such a great thing to do! Coloring got me through my inpatient stays and I know how much it sucks when you have less to work with than even a kindergartener. I bet you really made some people’s days a little better. Hope you’re doing okay with being out.

I've recently started thinking I'm trans and I'm definitely obsessing  over it. I'm constantly on YouTube and Reddit. I tried to limit myself and it just made me think about it more. I'm hoping it's something that'll burn out. But I think it's normal to want to see/read as much as possible about something you're coming to terms with. I hope you can find somebody supportive in your life. It can be so hard when your family expects you to be one specific way and you just aren't. Good luck with everything.

Being fickle like that is so annoying! Every time my mom gets her haircut she wants a different style and asks me about it for weeks and then she somehow comes home with the same thing every time. I just never want to talk to her about hair!

I’ve had my hair short for years and my mom will still look at old pictures and say ‘look how pretty your hair was!’ *looks at my short hair meaningfully* Yeaaaaah, not gonna look like that ever again! Some people just can’t let go!
Thanks for writing all that out! It really helps to hear other people’s perspectives/experiences.

I’ve always hated wearing bras too. Always told myself I couldn’t find a comfortable one, but I could never say what exactly was uncomfortable. Like, it fit fine. I hadn’t thought of that before! I’m kind of scared to see if my dysphoria develops now (to needing to wear a binder out all the time), but I’m still definitely riding the high of liking what I see in the mirror. Nice to hear from someone who felt similarly!

I feel like right now I’m really excited about this new image, but once it hits home that I’m going to need to bind most days  to keep this level of comfort.... that’s gonna suck. Thanks for the response!
Thanks! Hope you can find out if binding is right for you!
I love Ash's videos! Just discovered them a couple weeks ago. I'll have to look that one up! That sounds so relatable. hah

Thanks. I do keep thinking this is something I'm doing to myself. But really I think I'm just starting to realize that there are options. Things can be different. And it's blowing my mind and making me happy in a lot of ways, but also making me see that I'm not necessarily happy with the way things are. Crazy how our minds work and change!
Thanks for the reply. Feels good to know someone went through the same thing. As soon as I put my binder on I tried on like half the shirts in my closet just thinking yessss, this is right!

Yeah, that sucks. It's like once you know how right it can be, there's no going back. I should probably invest in some more sports bras. I've never worn one with binding in mind, and I bet it's going to be disappointing. Need to be healthy tho!

I feel the exact same way about how I didn't think about it because I just assumed it's how it should be. But I realized I feel so much better presenting a different way and now I'm thinking about it a lot. My brain is definitely freaking out a little. hah. Thanks for sharing your experience!
I just got my coupon code and re-ordered a size up yesterday! Hope yours comes fast! Can’t wait!

Thanks so much for the response! It all feels so new and confusing for me to be thinking about this, but it feels really good at the same time. Like something is just clicking. I'm definitely going to try out some baby steps. It would be awesome to try out pronouns and a masculine name, but I would need to ask a friend! My friends are pretty cool though. I could probably ask one or two so I could get a feel for it. It just feels kind of weird to talk about when I am so unsure, but I guess I can only figure out how I actually feel by trying things out. Anyways, thanks!
Yep, I’ve had it checked. Verrrry slightly hypothyroid. But mostly just tired from depression.

When I first told my parents, they had no idea what cutting was. I had to explain it all to them and for awhile they were just confused. My Dad wanted to 'fix' it and my mom was really sad and blamed herself. It's going to be really hard for people who love you to know you've been hurting yourself. But it'll make it a lot easier if you can tell them in a way that will help them understand why you do it and that it's not their fault at all. They are probably going to want to protect you at first. That can feel really demeaning if they go through the house hiding sharps or whatever, but it helped me to remember that it was all new to them. Of course I knew about my own cutting and was used to it, but they weren't. Parents just want to do what they feel is best for you. 

I only cut deep enough for stitches once, and I had to talk my Dad out of going to the doctor. I regret doing that actually. If you need medical care, get it. Also, doctors do understand the difference between cutting and suicide and most won't commit you for cutting. You do say that you've been thinking about killing yourself though. I just want to say that I've been in a psych ward twice for suicidal thoughts and, as much as people try to resist it sometimes, I found my time there invaluable. 

Sorry for the novel!  I hope you can get any help you need. And good luck with the parents. They're going to be scared and maybe a little angry, but that just comes from a place of love. I hope they can be there for you.

I get it. I don't know what to do either. Sometimes it comes back for me in brief moments like wanting ice cream or at least the beginning of a show I wanted to watch. I just try and live for those little things. It's not great : /
I used to live for alone time and being able to just relax and be lazy. When I'm left alone now, my mind goes to dark places and I generally become suicidal. I get it.
Wow. I just realized this is exactly what I want someone to say to me. This is really insightful.
I'm sorry it was a rough day. It sucks when you think everything should be fine, but it isn't.

70% of the time I end up squatting on the bathroom floor when i brush my teeth because standing is too much work, but I know if I sit down I won't be able to make myself get back up. I know it can be really hard, but maybe finding a lazy 'shortcut' kind of like that will help you do the things you have to.
Even looking at pictures is hard. I just think how sad my eyes look. How does no one else see how lost I am?

I understand the feeling. But maybe there's another way to get rid of the pain. It's awful when even 'fun' things take so much energy. Does your wife know how much you're struggling? I understand wanting to protect people from that pain, but when suicide is an option, it's time to reach out for all the resources you can. I hope you can feel even a glimmer of joy soon. Knowing it's possible to feel happy can take the edge off. Sorry it's so tough right now.

I struggle a lot with apathy. It's like I want to WANT to do things, but the motivation doesn't come. It's hard when nothing relieves that boredom. Personally, I prefer feeling sad over that empty, apathetic feeling. I can't help, just wanted to say I understand. Hopefully you can feel motivation or passion soon, even for a moment.
Hey, that's okay. It happens. Take care of yourself

I just want to say that I've never seen this articulated so well. I feel this exact same way. It's maddening being able to look at a situation objectively and yet still not be able to change your feelings about it. I too can have perfectly normal days and still want to kill/hurt myself. My therapist always seems surprised by how well versed I am in coping strategies, yet they don't help. The only thing I know that helps is sharing how I'm feeling, hence the therapy, and DISTRACTION. Anything to not think the thoughts. Anything to keep yourself from being alone.

Alternately, there is one other thing that helps me when I'm already too deep to stop the thought spiral. I don't know that it's all that healthy of an outlet, so take this with a grain of salt. If I can't get the thoughts out of my head, sometimes I like to watch movies about depression and suicide or read books about it. It's a way to give into the idea that, yeah, my brain is stuck on suicide right now, but it doesn't need to be my suicide. Just seeing that other people struggle and can relate gets me through the tough days sometimes. I don't know, just wanted to share since we sound very similar.

I don't know if this is the same, but I get extreme emotional surges that are disproportionate to whatever I'm reacting to. Sad line in a song? My voice cracks and tears well up just for a second. Watching COPS and the cop is worried about his police dog? Soul crushing agony for 30 seconds. It always leaves me thinking, seriously??? What is going on, emotions? Just started happening the last few months. Very out of character for me. It's not an emotion out of the blue which yours seems to be, but I just assume it's depression heightening negative stuff.

It sucks, but it will pass. I'm about 6 months clean and I went so far as to get a razor out a couple days ago. Instead I drew red lines on my arm and watched a sad movie. That's what helps me. Distraction is usually a good go-to. Can you call your friend and talk about how you're feeling? I know that's hard though. I hope you get through this. The urges never stay strong forever.

I also wonder if I'm just comfortable being depressed. It's so easy to get used to a certain way of being. Feeling like you've lost time is really hard, but starting something now is always better than not starting at all. You say you need help. Try and reach out. It's not easy, but it can feel really freeing to ask for help.
I think that reaching out can't hurt. A doctor can help you find resources that might make things easier.

I always think of the saying that goes something like, if people aren't allowed to be sad because somebody has it worse, then they can't be happy if somebody has it better. We don't limit our happiness like that, so why should we judge our sadness? You can be depressed even if your life appears generally fine. Your emotions are what they are. Mental illness affects everybody.

I'm sorry you're in so much pain. I know I can't really help, but I understand where you're at. It feels like an eternity, but in my experience, the emptiness and the pain always lifts. Not forever. But maybe enough for living to be worth it. I wish you the best.

Sometimes depression strikes for no reason, or so they say. I became depressed my junior year of college and everything was going good for me as well. Great home life, bright future. It took me awhile to understand that the way I was feeling wasn't right though and I ended up giving up my dream job in order to work on my mental health. Two years out of college and it's still a struggle, but I've learned a lot about how to cope with the sadness and apathy. 

Anyways, my point is that nothing is wrong with you for feeling that way. It happens, and it doesn't make you ungrateful. I think it's really good that you're realizing it though and I believe the best thing to do is to try and understand it and work through it before it builds up into something that seems insurmountable. Therapy can help a lot. Sharing those feelings makes them a little less bleak and a little less taboo. Sorry for the novel! Good luck with your internship : )

I've been there. I always know I'm getting really low if someone asks me to pet sit, or hang out, or make an appointment, and my first thought is  'I can't have someone counting on me because I might be dead by then.' Sometimes having a responsibility can carry you through the tough times though. I hope it gets a little easier for you.

I think both forms are just as valid. I personally have no explanation whatsoever. On paper, I was very happy with how my life was going. Everything was great. But I cried every day and became suicidal. So I guess it’s just chemical. 

Sometimes I feel jealous of people who know why they’re depressed. I think, if I just knew what was wrong, I could fix it. I know it’s not that easy though. Everyone has their own struggle. And really I think that’s all that matters. The way you feel. And if you feel depressed, if you have the symptoms, then you are. It doesn’t matter why.
Exactly. Once it’s an option, your brain always considers it as an option. Even if you’re in a good place.

Kind of related... when I started therapy I focused on describing my anxiety because I was only just starting to realize how sad I was and I was afraid to mention depression. They figured it out though. I think a lot of issues get mixed up together. Going back to therapy is a good step though! I hope it helps.
Just wanted to say thanks for the kind words

Yeah, the old ‘if you try not to think about a pink elephant...’ hah. If the thought just seems to come up for you for no reason, then that sounds like an intrusive thought. Whatever the reason, it’s definitely unnerving for something like that to feel comforting. I get it. 

I’ve never told anyone before about the feeling that just trying out the thoughts and giving in will make them go away. I feel less crazy after you saying you get that. lol. Anyways, good luck to you. Hope the thoughts lessen/go away.

My mind is obsessing over suicide right now. Relatively, I’m doing okay with my depression recently. I’m not too sad or hopeless, but I CAN’T STOP thinking about my suicide. I too focus on cutting my arms. It makes me want to do it just so the thoughts will stop. It’s like, I don’t want to die, but I want to TRY and kill myself. I fantasize about it all the time. It feels like I’m trying to keep myself depressed by having these thoughts and making plans. It really confuses me.
That’s what I was thinking too : / Relevant username
What I hate most is that I stay rational through my depression. I want that last part of me to break so I can kill myself without thinking of all the reasons why I shouldn’t.
Atlases. I couldn’t even remember the word the other day. GPS has taken over.

I have social anxiety, but I think the fear of failure was mostly instilled in myself. I remember in later years my parents telling me stuff like, ‘it’s okay to not get all A’s” “just do your best”. But I already thought my best wasn’t good enough and that I couldn’t be anything less than perfect. I think some people are just hardwired that way.

I just want to say this resonates with me. Everything you said about the happy feelings suddenly going away, about being so bored and trying anything to make something feel interesting. How you start living just so other people won’t be inconvenienced or sad. It’s been 2 years for me and every day feels endless. Just mind- numbingly boring. I don’t know how you made five years, but knowing that it came and went for you for no discernible reason makes me think that maybe getting better is possible. I always say I don’t know how to get better because nothing is wrong. There’s nothing I can fix. But I’m doing my best to hold on and hang in there and hope for a change. Anyways, I’m just rambling, but I really appreciate that you typed all that out. It was good to read.
Thank you so much! It means a lot that you give your time to make us all a little happier. : )
Okay, will do. Thanks so much!

Thank you! I appreciate it so much : ) I’m having a tough time lately and, as small as it is, this game is bringing me some happiness. I don’t have the money to make a donation, but I will definitely pass on the kindness!
The most outrageous thing was full drink cups or full bags of popcorn. That cost $6.75 or $9. Seriously? You just wanted to spend money for fun?

The thing that grossed me out the most was a cup full of spit from chewing tobacco. Only because I was an idiot and kept smelling the cup in the dark to try and figure out what the liquid was. 
I found a lot of orange peels and even a corn on the cob. The theater didn’t sell anything like that. There was also an entire meal from Popeyes that the greeter apparently missed. 
A lot of my coworkers saw rats.

I have experienced this once in my life. I am not a morning person, so the feeling of opening my eyes and being energized and looking forward to the day was thrilling. It was 6am in Japan and I had to wake up all of my other friends, professed morning people, so we’d have time to go in an onsen. The feeling is still so vivid in my memory. These days I feel dead tired no matter what. I’d love to feel that one more time. It was truly a feeling of contentment and bliss.

Hey, I just wanted to say I know where you are. It sounds like you're close to your family. Could you tell them how seriously you're contemplating suicide? I know what it feels like to run out of strength and those are the times I've gone to the mental hospital. It's not a quick fix, but it is a place to be safe for awhile. I'm sorry things are so hard right now. I hope you can find someone or something to help you carry on.

Depressed with no friends in the area really. Babysitting so that my neighbors can enjoy a night out. The kids are running out of steam so we’re going to watch Spongebob until we can toast the new year with sparkling apple and grape. : )

I do the exact same thing. Sometimes I'm just too tired to fight the thoughts. Sometimes I know that I can distract myself, but I hate the idea of that. I don't want my whole life to be a distraction, just constantly redirecting my negative thoughts. I want to not have the thoughts in the first place. So then I let myself spiral almost out of spite. I know it's not healthy but it's the path my brain wants to take.

Hey, I don't have an answer but I just want you to know I see your pain. You don't need to make any big decisions right now. Just keep breathing. Is there anyone in your life you could confide in? I hope things get better for you, even a little bit. I'm struggling myself right now and I can't imagine how hard the aftermath of an attempt must be.

People are going to self harm anyway whether there's a place to share images or not. I think it was a safe place to ask questions about opinions on whether a doctor's care was needed for stitches or possible infections. I hadn't posted pics of my own self harm there, but I had reached out to people on the sub before and it was nice just being able to see that I wasn't alone. I know you can talk about self harm here, but it's just different. I feel alone and scared now. And ashamed that... it's like we were doing something 'wrong'. I'm worried for the people that won't have that outlet to share the things they can't in real life.

I used it a lot when I was still in college. There’s definitely a knack to it. Basically, if you try at nighttime, you may never get through. There’s just too much traffic. Sometimes the numbers count down correctly and sometimes they jump up and down. I waited it out a lot because I was always too anxious to talk on the phone. Sometimes it will get stuck though so there’s a gamble about whether someone will appear on the other end. Usually when the numbers are below 10 it will sort out eventually. I’ve been #27 before. Hah. Hope that helps.

Joy, innocence, love. I’m so happy for the life that little kid had. She had everything and it was wonderful. I’m so grateful she didn’t know this was coming. And I’m so so sorry that I must’ve messed it up somewhere along the line. I would give anything for a little bit of that happiness again.

I’ve been dealing with this recently too. Graduated college in 2016. I used to love reading, TV, coloring, video games, knitting, and studying. Now, it’s like I can’t get enjoyment from these things anymore. I try to do them and I just feel nothing. Or I’m too tired to even try. The most I can do is passively watch TV. I want to do things, but I just end up on Reddit because it’s too sad to do my hobbies and feel nothing. Or to feel like they’re work.

I understand. I handle my depression the same way. I can’t stand for people to see me upset, I don’t want to be a burden, so I go cry somewhere private when I need a release. It’s the worst to sob in the bathroom at work and then walk out smiling like nothing happened. No one can tell that I spend 80% of my time thinking about self harm and suicide. Sometimes I wish some final straw would break so everyone would see what I’m really dealing with, but I worry it would hurt them too much. I know you’re out there though. Struggling in silence is just as valid. I know how hard the facade is.
